headline: Colder weather and higher gas rates lift results
summary_short: For the quarter ended March 31, 2026, UGI's net income rose 8.6% y/y to $520M ($2.33 diluted GAAP EPS) as revenue grew 0.7% y/y to $2,685M; adjusted (non-GAAP) diluted EPS was $2.09, down from $2.21 a year ago as lower Midstream & Marketing tax credits offset gains at Utilities, UGI International and AmeriGas Propane.
summary_long: GAAP net income benefited from $116M of net unrealized commodity/FX-derivative gains (vs. -$5M a year ago), partly offset by a $62M net loss on non-core LPG-business disposals. Utilities adjusted income rose $5M on higher total margin (PA base-rate increase, colder weather); UGI International rose $10M on lower income taxes; AmeriGas rose $60M on lower income taxes. Midstream & Marketing fell $41M on higher income-tax expense from lower investment tax credits. UGI International completed/agreed further non-core LPG divestitures (Romania closed; Czech/Hungary/Poland/Slovakia agreed, $64M impairment) and, after quarter-end, agreed to sell its Electric Utility for $470M. Total cash was $494M; equity was $5,419M. No forward guidance is stated in this 10-Q.

Utilities revenue +$107M on higher PGC/PGA and PA base rates plus off-system sales; Midstream & Marketing +$128M on higher natural gas marketing activity amid colder weather; partly offset by UGI International (-$29M, lower LPG volumes/prices) and AmeriGas (-$89M, lower propane volumes and selling prices).

Utilities operating income +$9M (higher total margin, partly offset by higher opex and depreciation); Midstream & Marketing -$6M (higher opex from renewable-energy projects); UGI International -$3M (lower total margin); AmeriGas +$2M (lower depreciation).
